summary: SSE handshake stall after auth cookie rotation strips trailing punctuation and image URLs from streamed markdown
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteWave Labs reports that during long-form SSE streams the final paragraphs frequently arrive with stripped trailing punctuation (periods and parentheses) and image markdown links (e.g., ![alt](https://...)) missing after an auth cookie rotation and fast reconnect. This results in corrupted markdown documents and broken image previews in their consumer app.

Impact:
- Several NoteWave production users receive incomplete markdown: sentences end abruptly without closing punctuation and the final image references are dropped.
- Breaks client-side markdown renderer resulting in UI glitches and broken card previews.
- Appears intermittently following auth cookie refresh during long SSE sessions behind the customer's CDN.

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1, customer requests served from our hosted Redwood API cluster on redwood-dedicated-01.
- Affected routes: /v1/streams/generate and chat streaming endpoints.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1. Start a long SSE stream request that outputs markdown with an embedded image near the end.
2. While the stream is active, NoteWave's edge rotates their SSO cookie (short TTL) triggering the client to re-auth and re-open the SSE connection.
3. Client performs an immediate reconnect; upstream CDN uses HTTP/1.1 keepalive and replays a 100-continue probe in front of the handshake.
4. After reconnect completes, the last paragraph is missing trailing punctuation (usually "." or ")") and the markdown image URL is omitted.

Expected behavior:
- Stream should resume or fall back without losing trailing characters or image references. Final tokens and markdown should stitch cleanly.

Observed behavior:
- The stream resumes but the final chunk is missing the terminal characters and the entire markdown image link token sequence. The rest of the output appears intact.

Immediate customer-provided logs (redacted):
- Client-side SSE events show final data chunk as: "...conclusion of thought\n\n![diagram]" (image URL missing)
- Server-side proxied access logs show a timed cookie refresh and a 100-continue preflight from the CDN within 120ms of the reconnect.
- No 5xx from runtime; serving runtime logs show an ACK for last-KV-cache priming followed by a short-lived socket replacement.

Attachments:
- customer_trace_2026-03-09.zip (contains client SSE sequence and server access logs)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported broken image links and missing trailing punctuation after a cookie refresh mid-stream. Provided initial traces and requested escalation.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced locally behind our staging CDN emulator; observed identical missing token behavior when a synthetic 100-continue probe is injected during socket handoff. Captured pcap and stack traces.

2026-03-10 11:40 - Platform Eng (Lina Chen): Hypothesis: edge-proxy reorder + inflight 100-continue causes our streaming chunk assembler to treat the following resume as a fresh stream boundary, dropping the last few bytes that were buffered as 'prelude'. Added logging around stream boundary state.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer confirmed issue occurs ~3% of long sessions (10k+ tokens) with their CDN. They can reproduce reliably by toggling SSO cookie TTL to short values. Customer asks for a hotfix because these are marketing cards that rely on image rendering.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Reproducible when a reconnect happens within 200ms of an auth cookie rotation and when an intermediate CDN sends a 100-continue or idle probe during handshake.
- The streaming runtime's chunk reassembly state machine expects a clearly delimited 'end-of-chunk' marker. During the handshake replay, a small buffered suffix (1-6 bytes) containing punctuation or the tail end of a markdown image token is being classified as 'prelude' and not appended to the prior choice.
- Edge-proxy logs show connection rebinds that reorder control bytes; our parser currently treats an immediate SYN/HTTP1 probe sequence as a boundary and flushes partial token buffers.
- Affected models are token-dense near stream ends (long-form markdown with links) which increases chance of tail bytes alignment.
- No evidence of model truncation or tokenization loss inside the runtime; this is an I/O/assembler issue.

Next steps proposed:
1) Add conservative reassembly window: when a reconnect occurs within X ms of the prior stream tail, retain the last 12 bytes of buffer and attempt to stitch if subsequent resume begins with an open markdown bracket or punctuation. (short-term patch)
2) Harden handshake handling in edge-proxy to avoid treating 100-continue as stream boundary. (medium-term)
3) Add end-to-end test scenario with injected 100-continue / CDN probes to catch regressions.
4) Coordinate with customer to test a canary patch that preserves trailing bytes in stitch path.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds and fixes in progress:
- Temporary customer workaround: increase SSO cookie TTL for long-run streams (reduces rotation events mid-stream). Customer applied and reported reduction in occurrences to near 0 during test window.
- Engineering hotfix (in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-runtime/pull/410) introduces a 12-byte stitch buffer on reconnect and adds heuristic to merge if next chunk starts with markdown markers or typical trailing punctuation.
- Edge-proxy change (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-gateway/pull/205) updates probe handling so 100-continue is not treated as an SSE boundary.
- Added a regression test to CI that simulates cookie rotation + 100-continue scenario.

Pending:
- Awaiting customer validation in their staging CDN by 2026-03-13. If validation passes, schedule hotfix roll to prod in a limited canary (5% of traffic) with observability flags enabled.
resolution: Fix in progress (stitch-buffer patch + proxy probe handling). Customer workaround applied and validated on staging. Pending customer sign-off for prod rollout.
notes: Do not change tokenizer or model weights as this is an I/O boundary case.
Ensure canary includes both redwood-small-13b and open-llama-7b traffic to validate model-agnostic behavior.
